content:
acme-sre: Hey team — after rotating IdP signing certs last night some of our users started getting 403s during SSO. Happens intermittently, ~30% of logins. Not seeing clear errors on our side, can you help triage?

samir: @acme-sre thanks, can you paste the SAML response (or at least the Recipient/AssertionConsumerServiceURL) and any prod nginx proxy logs you have?

acme-sre: Here's one SAML Response excerpt from a failed login (redacted):
```xml
<samlp:Response ...>
  <saml:Assertion>
    <saml:SubjectConfirmationData Recipient="https://app.acme.com/saml/acs" NotOnOrAfter="2026-11-12T12:03:00Z" ... />
  </saml:Assertion>
</samlp:Response>
```
Request to our ACS returned 403 with message: `recipient not allowed`.

marta: Curious — our ACS handler canonicalizes the URL and we expect no trailing slash. In your config the ACS is `/saml/acs` (no trailing slash) — do you have any proxy rewrite?

acme-sre: We do have an edge proxy in front (nginx) that adds `X-Forwarded-Proto` and rewrites host. Here's the relevant snippet: 
```nginx
proxy_set_header Host $host;
proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-For $remote_addr;
proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-Proto $scheme;
proxy_pass http://internal-app;
```
We also have an auth layer that normalizes URLs and sometimes appends a trailing slash.

devops-bot: Deploy completed for idp cert rotate at 2026-11-12T02:10Z. Noted both old and new certs were in metadata for a few hours.

samir: Two hypotheses: 1) The IdP's metadata still contains old cert and some IdP instances sign with old key -> signature invalid vs our expected key, 2) The ACS Recipient in SAML response doesn't match the exact URL we registered (trailing slash / scheme mismatch) — SAML strict match fails.

acme-sre: We matched metadata and saw the new cert in the IdP console. But we discovered our ACS URL in the SP config is `https://app.acme.com/saml/acs/` (trailing slash) while the Assertion used `https://app.acme.com/saml/acs` (no slash). Could that explain 30% failures?

marta: Yep — SAML recipients are often strict. If you have multiple IdP nodes, some might use one variant. Also note if X-Forwarded-Proto is `http` while we expect `https` the built absolute URL in some libs can pick the wrong scheme.

samir: Quick repro: curl the assertion consumer with a dummy POST and check our SP rejects Recipient mismatch. Example: 
```bash
curl -v -H 'X-Forwarded-Proto: http' -H 'Host: app.acme.com' -X POST 'http://internal-app/saml/acs' --data-binary @saml_response.xml
```
If the internal app constructs ACS as `http://app.acme.com/saml/acs/` you can see the mismatch.

acme-sre: Running that now, I see logs where internal request shows scheme `http` and code path appended a slash. Repro confirmed: `Recipient mismatch: expected https://app.acme.com/saml/acs/ got https://app.acme.com/saml/acs`

elaine: For mitigation you can (1) make SP accept both variants by relaxing strict recipient check temporarily, (2) normalize ACS to a single canonical value and update SP metadata, and (3) ensure proxy forwards `X-Forwarded-Proto: https` when terminating TLS at edge.

marta: Also ensure the IdP metadata contains both signing certs during rotation window. If some IdP nodes still sign with old key and you removed it early, signatures will fail. Check the `KeyInfo` thumbprint in failed assertions.

acme-sre: Thumbprint check shows some responses signed with the old cert fingerprint `AB:12:CD:34:EF` — but we added the new cert last-night and removed old one at 04:00Z. Looks like some IdP nodes were still issuing tokens with old cert.

samir: That explains the intermittent nature. Two parallel fixes: restore old cert to metadata for a short window (or re-add both), and canonicalize ACS + proxy headers. I can open a short-lived allowlist for the old thumbprint while you coordinate IdP rollout.

acme-sre: We re-added old cert to metadata on IdP and updated nginx to force `proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-Proto https;` for upstream internal-app.

marta: After those changes, can you run a smoke test (few logins) and paste results?

acme-sre: Smoke test: 20 logins — 0 failures. Looks green. We'll monitor for a couple hours and then rotate IdP nodes more carefully. Thanks! :partyparrot: 

triage: Marking as resolved for now. Please reopen if the 403s come back or you re-roll certs.

samir: Follow-up notes: - Document canonical ACS URL in SP metadata (no trailing slash) - Add a pre-rotation checklist to keep both certs in IdP metadata for X hours - Ensure proxies set correct `X-Forwarded-Proto` when TLS terminated at edge

acme-sre: Adding those to our runbook now. Appreciate the help.
